title: eval-harness: add per-prompt regression CI hook + quality gating for prompt-set v2
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Adds a per-prompt regression CI hook and quality gating for the new prompt-set v2. Motivation: several regressions slipped through the model rollout for chat-completion in late 2025 because evals were coarse-grained and expensive. This change introduces a lightweight per-prompt runner that executes a targeted subset of evals as a CI hook, computes per-prompt deltas against baseline metrics stored in the eval registry, and fails the CI if configurable thresholds for pass-rate drop or metric regression are exceeded. Key parts: (1) per-prompt runner and sharding (parallelized across CI agents); (2) new quality gating config with thresholds and hard/soft failure modes; (3) integration with metrics exporter so CI logs show per-prompt metrics and links to evaluations in the console; (4) caching of stable eval outputs to reduce runtime; (5) doc updates and unit/integration tests. Backwards compatible: hook is opt-in via repo-level .eval-config.yaml and enabled by default for prompt-set v2. See linked Linear tickets ENG-1245 and ENG-2011 for rollout plan and threshold tuning.
commits: feat(eval): add per-prompt ci hook runner and shard orchestration
perf(eval): parallelize prompt execution across CI workers and add in-memory caching
feat(config): add .eval-config.yaml schema and default quality gates for prompt-set v2
chore(tests): add unit tests for gating logic and integration test that simulates regression
docs: document per-prompt hook behavior and troubleshooting guide
review_comments: Avery Morris: Nice end-to-end. Two requests: (1) make the default gate conservative (0.5% absolute drop) until we see stability, (2) add a flag to run full eval-suite in case of flaky CI failures.
Priya Kapoor (author): Addressed both — default gates lowered to conservative values and added --run-full-suite override to the hook. Added tests that exercise the override.
Diego Ramos: Found a race in shard_executor when multiple workers update the cache simultaneously. Recommend using file-lock fallback for the shared cache in CI.
Priya Kapoor (author): Fixed race by switching to atomic write/tempfile pattern and added a retry. Added comments explaining the design decisions and trade-offs.
Sunita Patel: Can we expose the gating summary as a short JSON artifact for the CI UI? This would make triage easier.
Priya Kapoor (author): Added a succinct gating-summary.json output and a link printed in CI logs.
ci_checks: ci/integration: fail (flake in runner on first run) -> rerun -> pass
ci/eval-hook-smoke: pass (hook runtime ~ 4m with cache, 15m without cache on oxci agents)
merge_commit: squash: feat(eval): per-prompt ci hook + gating (Priya Kapoor)\n\nCo-authored-by: Avery Morris <avery@redwood.com>
release_notes:
- Added per-prompt regression CI hook to run lightweight evals on PRs and enforce quality gates.
- Default quality gates are conservative for prompt-set v2; configurable via .eval-config.yaml.
- Outputs gating-summary.json artifact for easier triage and links to full evals in the console.
- Performance: average hook run-time reduced via caching and parallel execution.
- No breaking changes; opt-in via config.
